    JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND
        LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR
    CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY
      EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE
                                            PROJECT
          BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS

     CONSOLIDATED STATEMENT OF POSITION AND POST-HEARING BRIEF

     OF LOREN & CHARLES POWELL, PRO SE, ON BEHALF OF ORAN CREEK
                            RANCH LLC

                  I. INTRODUCTION AND STATEMENT OF POSITION

We, Loren and Charles Powell, appear pro se on behalf of Oran Creek Ranch LLC, the owner of
approximately 300 acres of long-undisturbed ranchland directly affected by the proposed G-6
segment ofthe Bell County East to Big Hill 765-kV transmission line.

We respect that the Commission' s statutory role is to select a route, not to redesign Texas' s
energy policy. However, PURA requires the Commission to determine whether the record
supports the necessity and appropriateness ofthis specific project, and whether the proposed
route satisfies the statutory requirements of least-impact routing, community values,
environmental integrity, and landowner protection.

Our exhibits, included in our original testimony filed in PUC Docket No. 59475 as item no.
3800, provide photographs, maps, and narrative evidence showing the severe and
disproportionate impacts the proposed G-6 route would impose on our home, viewshed, and
ranch operations.

For these reasons, we respectfully request that the Commission reject the G-6 segment and select
a less-intrusive alternative.

                        II. SUBSTANTIAL EVIDENCE STANDARD

Texas courts require agency decisions to be supported by "such relevant evidence as a reasonable
mind might accept as adequate to support a conclusion."




SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 / PUC Docket No. 59475
1
POWELL STATEMENT OF POSITION AND POST-HEARING BRIEF
 However:

• Conclusory statements are not substantial evidence. • Expert opinions unsupported by
underlying data cannot support an agency decision. • Agencies may not rely on testimony that
merely asks the tribunal to "trust" the expert. • Agencies must consider all relevant factors and
cannot rely on incomplete analysis.

The Commission must apply these principles here.

                              III. HEALTH AND SAFETY IMPACTS

During the hearing, the Applicants' medical and health expert, Dr. Gelman, admitted that he had
conducted no research whatsoever regarding EMF exposure or potential health impacts
associated with 765-kV transmission lines. He further acknowledged that he was not familiar
with peer-reviewed studies by other researchers that raise concerns about possible health effects
from high-voltage transmission infrastructure.

When he was asked about potential or dangerous health impacts on humans, wildlife, or
livestock, Dr. Gelman was dismissive. He stated that his laboratory work with rodents did not
lead him to those conclusions, even though his rodent studies were not conducted at 765-kV field
strengths, nor were they designed to evaluate the unique EMF characteristics of a line of this
magnitude.

Instead of providing empirical data, project-specific analysis, or peer-reviewed research, Dr.
Gelman ultimately asked the Commission to trust his judgment based solely on his professional
stature as a medical researcher.

This is the first 765-kV line in Texas, with no historical health-impact record. Without empirical
evidence, peer-reviewed research, or project-specific analysis, the Commission cannot
reasonably conclude that siting a 765-kV line within 500 feet of our residence poses no health
risk to us, to wildlife, or to livestock.

                     IV. ROUTING IMPACTS ON ORAN CREEK RANCH

Oran Creek Ranch is an approximately 300-acre, multi -parcel, long-undisturbed ranch that has
remained intact for generations. Its value derives from its cohesive landscape, unbroken
viewshed, wildlife habitat, and functional unity as a working ranch.

The revised G-6 alignment no longer bisects the ranch diagonally, but the new configuration is
equally - and in some respects more - harmful. The current route:



SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 / PUC Docket No. 59475
2
POWELL STATEMENT OF POSITION AND POST-HEARING BRIEF
 • runs from the front to the back of the ranch along two parcels, • passes approximately 500 feet
in front of our residence, • sits directly within our home' s primary viewshed, • permanently
destroys the scenic and aesthetic value ofthe property, • introduces a 765-kV industrial corridor
into an otherwise undisturbed landscape, • fragments pastures and wildlife movement patterns, •
creates long-term ecological disturbance across multiple parcels.

The exhibits in our original testimony from PUC Docket No. 59475 as item no. 3800 include
photographs of the viewshed, maps showing the alignment relative to our home, and
documentation of the wildlife preservation as well as the ongoing stewardship of our ranch.

Former PUC Chairman Barry Smitherman, while under oath and testifying at the hearing as an
expert witness, emphasized that previously undisturbed ranchlands should not be violated when
reasonable alternatives exist. Oran Creek Ranch is exactly the type of property he described.

Routing a new 765-kV greenfield corridor through such land, especially within 500 feet of a
residence, is inconsistent with PURA § 37.056(c)(4)'s requirement to minimize landowner
impacts.

                                  V. COMMUNITY VALUES

PURA requires the Commission to consider community values, including:

• preservation of rural landscapes, • protection of undisturbed ranchlands, • avoidance of
disproportionate burdens on individual landowners, • respect for long-established land
stewardship.

The revised G-6 alignment violates these values by placing a 765-kV line directly in front of our
home, within approximately 500 feet, and running the length ofthe ranch along two parcels. This
alignment destroys the primary viewshed, undermines the rural character of the property, and
imposes the most severe visual and residential impacts possible.

The exhibits in our original testimony from PUC Docket No. 59475 as item no. 3800 include
documentation of community values, rural character, and long-standing land stewardship in the
surrounding area.

                            VI. ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRITY

The revised G-6 alignment would:

           Run the length of the ranch from front to back,
           Pass approximately 500 feet in front of our residence,
           Fragment wildlife corridors and habitat continuity,
           Impair riparian areas and natural drainage patterns,
           Introduce industrial infrastructure into a previously undisturbed landscape,

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 / PUC Docket No. 59475
3
POWELL STATEMENT OF POSITION AND POST-HEARING BRIEF
             Create long-term ecological disturbance across multiple parcels.

Our original testimony in PUC Docket No. 59475 as item no. 3800 includes documentation of
wildlife activity, riparian features, and environmental stewardship practices that demonstrate the
ecological sensitivity of the ranch.

PURA § 37.056(c)(5) requires the Commission to protect environmental integrity. The G-6
alignment fails this requirement by imposing unnecessary environmental harm on intact ranchland
when less-intrusive alternatives exist.

                      VII. FAILURE TO CONSIDER ALTERNATIVES

During the hearing, several intervenors questioned why Oncor did not evaluate generation-based
alternatives, hybrid solutions, or upgrades to existing 345-kV corridors before proposing a new
765-kV greenfield route. In response to these questions, Mr. Rasmusson, counsel for Oncor,
stated on the record that Oncor is "in the transmission business, not the oil and gas business."

This statement is significant. It confirms that Oncor did not evaluate alternatives not because
they were infeasible, but because they fell outside of Oncor' s preferred business model. PURA
does not allow a utility to avoid evaluating reasonable alternatives simply because they are not
part of its corporate focus.

PURA requires the Applicant to demonstrate that the proposed project is the least-cost,
least-impact solution. A utility cannot satisfy that burden by declining to evaluate alternatives
because they fall outside its business model.

Routing a 765-kV line within 500 feet of a residence on a long-undisturbed ranch - without
evaluating alternatives - is inconsistent with PURA and Texas case law requiring agencies to
consider all relevant factors.

                      VIII. CONCLUSION AND REQUESTED RELIEF

For the reasons stated above, we, Loren and Charles Powell, pro se on behalf of Oran Creek
Ranch LLC, respectfully request that the Commission:

    1. Reject the G-6 segment due to its disproportionate impacts on undisturbed ranchlands,
       failure to satisfy PURA's least-impact requirement, and lack of substantial evidence
       supporting its necessity.
    2. Select a less-intrusive alternative route that avoids intact ranchlands and minimizes
       landowner impacts.
    3. Decline to rely on conclusory expert testimony unsupported by peer-reviewed research or
       independent analysis.
    4. Require a complete evaluation of reasonable alternatives before approving a project of
       this magnitude.
